page: Amazon Web Services c6in.large is a network-enhanced compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor based on the x86_64 architecture, providing 2 vCPUs mapped across a single physical core with hyper-threading. The underlying hardware incorporates 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 54 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside hardware instruction support for AVX-512, cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI, and BMI2 instructions. The instance is paired with 4.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing an allocation ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Network throughput is provisioned with a 3 Gbps baseline, while persistent storage must be mounted externally via EBS, as no bundled local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU silicon is included.

Empirical benchmarks reflect the distinct characteristics of the single-core physical allocation. Single-threaded metrics, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1565.0, a stress-ng single-core rating of 1880.89, single-threaded gzip compression at 27.7 GB/s, and bzip3 decompression at 9.95 GB/s, place the instance squarely within middle-tier industry averages. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics scale proportionally to its two-thread limit, posting 1810.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 1920.38 in stress-ng multi-core testing. Memory bandwidth registers at 13.88 GB/s for uncached reads and 12.88 GB/s for writes, reflecting standard dual-thread memory bus constraints. Extended compute scenarios, such as PassMark integer and floating-point tests, remain modest in absolute scale due to the entry-level core count.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the c6in.large delivers dedicated hardware threads and high baseline network throughput at an entry-tier resource footprint. The lack of integrated ephemeral storage and moderate memory capacity make it unsuited for large memory-resident caching, in-memory databases, or intense multi-core compilation. Instead, the architectural balance between reliable 3.5 GHz clock rates and 3 Gbps networking makes it an effective deployment target for lightweight web reverse proxies, API microservices, distributed cluster worker agents, and entry-level ETL pipelines that prioritize network capability over massive core parallelism.
description: Amazon Web Services c6in.large is a network-optimized, compute-focused virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. Configured on the Nitro hypervisor, the instance delivers two dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyper-threading enabled, accompanied by 4.0 GB of DDR4 system memory. It does not include local instance storage or GPU acceleration, relying on remote EBS volumes for persistent disk storage, while offering a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. Benchmark results demonstrate average single-threaded performance in gzip compression, bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench single-core execution. However, aggregate multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth fall into the lower tiers due to the constrained two-vCPU footprint. The c6in.large provides resource efficiency for network-sensitive, lightweight compute tasks, microservices, small API gateways, static web proxying, and background batch workers requiring predictable single-thread execution without intensive multi-core processing or heavy memory residency.
